newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen in negotiations for release of U.S. hostage.
newsitem.headline: Yemen in negotiations for release of U.S. hostage.

text.p: Yemeni security forces have laid siege on mountain tribesmen holding a U.S. oil engineer hostage in the rugged interior of the country, security sources said on Tuesday.

Joe D'ellaire, an engineer working for the U.S. engineering group Halliburton, was abducted on February 10 in Yemen's eastern Marib governorate by members of the Murad tribe, angered by a dispute over land.

The sources said the kidnappers were demanding compensation of $2 million or the return of a piece of land in the capital Sanaa they say was given to one of the tribal leaders, Sheikh Abdullah Abdrabu al-Mansouri.
"The al-Juba district in the governorate of Marib has been under siege since late Sunday night," one source told Reuters.
The kidnappers, who are followers of Sheikh Abdullah, say the land near the presidential palace had been donated to the tribal leader and later taken back by the Sanaa municipality.
Other leaders of the Murad tribe were now negotiating with Sheikh Abdullah's followers for the release of the American engineer, sources close to the negotiations said.
They did not say whether the other tribal chiefs were leading the talks on behalf of the government.
D'ellaire was abducted from Rig 1 on the Saad al-Kamel oilfield, about 300 km (185 miles) east of Sanaa, oil industry officials said.
He had been one of 125 men stationed on the rig, they said.
In recent years, Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners as bargaining chips.
The hostages, who have included an oil man from the private U.S. company Hunt Oil and another from U.S. oil services company Nabors Industries Inc, have all been released unharmed.
